clean: Hi Ruth, I'm writing from the hospital cafeteria because the internet in Dad's room is terrible. The surgery went well. The doctor came out at about 2 and said everything looked clean and he should be walking by tomorrow afternoon, which I find hard to believe, but okay. Dad is groggy and keeps asking if the dog has been fed. I've told him five times that she reason. Mom is a wreck but she's pretending she isn't, so I'm making her eat something every couple of hours. The nurse says visiting hours end at 8, so I'll be here till then, and if you want to call, the best time is probably around 7, when he's had dinner and isn't asleep. I'll put you on speaker. Don't bring up the golf trip, he's still sore about it. I'll write again tomorrow.

Dear Grandma and Grandpa, thank you so much for the parcel. The kids opened it at breakfast and nearly lost their minds. Lena is wearing the red scarf to bed, which I'm choosing not to fight, and Thomas has already read the dinosaur book twice. He's obsessed with the stegosaurus. School is going well. Lena has her first spelling test on Friday and she's been practicing in the bath. Thomas lost his first tooth last week, and the tooth fairy got confused and left a two dollar coin and a note saying sorry, which I'm told is not standard. We're planning to visit in April, hopefully the second week. I'll confirm once I've checked with work. Lots of love, Anna

Marcus, congratulations, I mean it. I read your message three times and I'm still grinning. A girl, and 8 pounds 2 ounces, that's a proper size. How's Rebecca doing? I hope she's getting some sleep. I know she won't be. I remember when ours were born, we didn't sleep for a month and I put the car keys in the fridge twice. Anyway, we want to bring over some food, lasagna, soup, whatever you'd like. Just tell us what you need and what you don't, and we promise not to stay long. I know the first week is a lot. If you'd rather have no visitors that's totally fine, just say the word. Give her a kiss from us, and a very small hat. I knitted one, it's yellow, it's terrible, I'm sorry in advance. With all our love, Nina and Andrew

Okay everyone, if I could have your attention, I promise this will be short. Andre, my little brother, who is not little anymore, is 40 today, and I want to say a few things. When we were kids he once ate an entire birthday cake because he thought it was his. It wasn't, it was mine. He's never apologized. He cried for an hour when I left for college, and then he sold my bike. I found out two years later. He's the most generous person I know, and the worst at keeping a secret. He told me what he was getting me for Christmas every single year. Here's to 40, here's to the next 40, and here's to the cake. Please nobody eat it before we sing.

Hello darling, it's Grandma. I am calling because I tried to use the new tablet you gave me and I pressed something and now everything is very big. The letters are enormous. I can only see three words on the screen. I called your uncle and he said to go to settings, but I cannot find the settings. There is a little picture of a gear, is that it? I pressed it and it made a noise. Now the screen has gone black. I think I have broken it. Please don't be angry. I am going to put it in the drawer and wait for you to come on Sunday. Bring the cable, and some of that nice cheese you bought last time, the one with the blue. I will make tea. Bye darling, kiss kiss.

Hi Andre, you mentioned your broker was good and I wanted to ask for her details. We've been renting for eight years and finally think we can buy. We've saved about $40,000, which doesn't sound like much but it's taken us forever, and our credit scores are fine, I think. Mine is 740 and my wife's is 710. The problem is I'm self-employed, so the banks keep asking for two years of statements, and I only have 19 months, because I started in February of the year before last. So I was hoping someone who knows the system could tell us whether it's worth trying now or whether we should wait. I don't want to waste your time. I'll pay for a consultation if that's how it works. Let me know, thanks a lot, Amara

I need to tell you about the worst haircut of my life. I went to this new place, because my usual guy retired, and I said just a trim. I even showed her a photo, and she nodded and smiled, and then she started cutting and I realized she was cutting a lot, a lot, and I'm sitting there frozen, because what are you supposed to say? And by the time she finished I had a bowl cut. I'm 34 years old, I look like a mushroom. I paid, I tipped, I said thank you. I'm a coward. And now I'm wearing a hat. I'm going to wear a hat until it grows back, which is going to be a while, so if you see me at work and I'm in a hat, don't ask, just nod.

When you go to the store, can you grab a few things for the party? We need three bags of ice, it's going to be hot, a big watermelon, napkins, the paper ones, not the ones with the pattern, the birthday candles, not the scented ones, a lighter, and some of those little forks for the cake. Oh, and chips, any kind but not the spicy ones because my mom can't handle them. I'll pay you back when you get here, and if they have those colorful straws, grab a pack. The kids will love them. Thank you, you're the best brother.

Hi, you asked for book recommendations for the flight, so here goes. I'd start with the one about the shipwreck. It's long but you can't put it down. Then there's the short story collection by that Irish writer, the one with the blue cover, which is perfect for turbulence because each story is only 10 pages. And finally, if you want something light, the new mystery from the woman who writes the cat detectives. It's silly and sweet. I read it in a day. I'll order all three from the bookstore and have them sent to your house. Don't argue, it's my treat. Safe travels, let me know what you think. Sending hugs.

Okay, house meeting thoughts. The kitchen is a crime scene. There's a pot in the sink that has been there since Monday, and I know it's not mine because I don't own a pot that color. I'm not angry, I'm just disappointed. Can we agree on a rota? I'll take the bins and the bathroom, Not ya can do the floors, and whoever cooks doesn't wash up, the others do. I'm making a chart and sticking it on the fridge, don't fight me on it. Also, somebody keeps eating my yogurt. I've labeled it, twice. I'm not naming names, but his name is Sam.

Happy anniversary, my love. I was thinking this morning about the day we met. You were holding three coffees because your friends had bailed on you, and you spilled one on my shoes, and I said it's fine, and you said it's not fine, those are very nice shoes, and I fell in love a little bit right there. I know that sounds like a movie, and it kind of was. And I wouldn't change it. I booked a table at that little Italian place for 7, the one with the candles in bottles. Don't make plans, wear the green dress, I'll pick you up at 6:30. I love you, more than the shoes, more than the coffee. Thanks for putting up with me.

I want you to act as a sceptical loan officer. I'm going to paste in a small business loan application next and I want you to read it the way a tough underwriter would. Look for gaps in the cash flow, anything that doesn't add up between the tax returns and the projections, and any red flags in the debt to income ratio. Don't be polite about it. After that, rewrite the weakest section so it's stronger but keep it honest, and tell me what supporting documents I should attach. Start by asking me anything you need to know about the business.

My team is kind of drowning in follow up emails and I want to build a prompt template we can all reuse. The template should take a prospect's name, and then write a follow up that's under 120 words. It should sound like a person wrote it, not like a robot, so no phrases like I hope this email finds you well. Include one clear next step and a link placeholder for booking time. Can you write the template and then show me an example using a fake prospect named Dana at some company called Bright Path?

I'm writing an email to my cooking class students about the canceled session and I want you to draft it. The reason is the instructor, that's me, broke my wrist on Sunday, so I can't hold a knife for about three weeks. I feel terrible about it, I mean it. Offer them either a refund or a credit toward the next series, and tell them the decision is due by the end of the month. Warm tone, short paragraphs, and don't make it sound like a legal notice. Sign it Diminick.
